description: Build provenance for the RT-BE Series 'Reaper' firmware. Each published image is traceable to an exact, independently-reproducible source tree: apply the published patch series onto the pinned upstream base, then hash release/src/router. The CI workflow .github/workflows/verify-provenance.yml reproduces every 'verifiable' entry on each run.

base.note: The base pin never moves. Reaper changes are carried as the patches/ series, and upstream carry-forwards (e.g. Merlin 3006.102.8 -> v2.1.2) are cherry-picked, NOT rebased, so this base stays constant and the reproduction recipe below is stable across releases.
base.series_note: Applying the published patches/ series from this base reproduces every release's source. Two hashes are recorded per release: source_tree is the tree of the build commit on the RT-BE96U branch (what the firmware was actually built from); source_tree_from_series is what `git am --keep-cr patches/[0-9]*.patch` onto this base yields. They differ ONLY by three vendored openssh-sftp documentation files (README.md, SECURITY.md, .github/ci-status.md) that the series' *.md doc-hunk exclusion strips; no source or code file differs, and release/src-rt is identical. CI (verify-provenance.yml) checks source_tree_from_series.

toolchain.note: Bit-for-bit binary reproduction additionally requires the proprietary Broadcom/ASUS/Trend Micro prebuilt blobs that upstream ships in-tree and that cannot be re-hosted here; the SOURCE reproduction (release/src/router tree hash) is fully independent of them.

reproduce: git clone https://github.com/RMerl/asuswrt-merlin.ng && cd asuswrt-merlin.ng && git checkout a7ebfa133a && git am --keep-cr /path/to/patches/0001-*.patch .. /path/to/patches/<NNNN>-*.patch && git rev-parse HEAD:release/src/router  # == the release's source_tree['release/src/router']

releases.summary: Stock ASUS wanduck Dual WAN fail-back loop fixed (246baa51b8). In fb mode the primary's changed_count[] doubles as the fail-back counter while the backup is active (counts to wandog_fb_count, default 4); the return-to-primary block called switch_wan_line(primary, 0) without resetting it, so the primary became the current line at or above wandog_maxfail (default 2, interval 3 s). With conn_state_old[primary] still DISCONN from the original outage, one DISCONN scan right after fail-back (default route not yet moved; restart_wan_line is not waited on) took the DISCONN branch: switch_wan_line(backup, 1), whose restart_other loop issues restart_wan_if <primary> and kills the fresh PPPoE session, repeating on every return. Unplugging the backup masked it (a disconnected primary is not counted while the other line has no link). Fix: set_disconn_count(primary, S_IDLE) after the fail-back switch. Field report GT-BE98 v3.2.6 (PPPoE on WAN, LAN-port WAN backup). Built and verified locally as an RT-BE96U MCP test image (reaper_verify 34/0/0); reporter confirmation on metal owed.

releases.summary: A Policy Routing source rule to a WireGuard client target now carries the replies home. rc/reaper_pbr.c: the rule marked the flow's first packet and saved the mark on the conntrack entry as intended, but the REAPER_PBR PREROUTING jump has no -i, so the REPLY arriving on wgcN had the same mark restored and was routed by lookup wgcN; under MULTILAN_CFG that table holds only 0/1 and 128/1 dev wgcN with no LAN route, so the reply went back into the tunnel. The chain now opens with -m conntrack --ctdir REPLY -j RETURN in both families, ahead of the restores and the trailing --save-mark (scoping only the restores would let an unmarked reply save 0 over the flow's verdict); replies route by main, as VPN Director's do, and wgcN rp_filter is loose. OpenVPN targets (their tables carry the LAN route) and VPN Director (its from <src> rule never matches a reply) were unaffected. reaper_fwsim models --ctdir, so the new rule is a modelled row. Root cause from a tester capture on an RT-BE86U; reproduced in a network-namespace model (without the rule 0/10 pings answered, with it 10/10). Metal confirmation from the reporter owed. No local image was built for this rung; it ships inside v3.2.5.

releases.summary: A locked cell on Wireless > Settings (www/Reaper_WiFiSettings.asp) says why on hover: setHardLock(el, locked, force, why) sets the cell's title to the reason while the lock holds and removes it when it lifts, and a WHY map (RWFP_67-82, plus RWFP_49 for the auto-channel cell) covers every lock the page applies - MLO holding the radio on, Legacy mode, WMM as a choice in Legacy only, MU-MIMO derived from OFDMA, the fixed-channel park, AMPDU RTS off, pre-emptive Bluetooth, the scheduler under MLO, Disable 802.11b as the preamble master. Greyed stays the only visible signal. Four-radio tester fixes on the same page: numeric boxes span the cell like the selects, the unit inside the box (.numwrap.hasunit); an nvram key rendered in two columns on a box with two 5 GHz radios (the DFS and U-NII-4 auto-channel options, data-g) is mirrored on change, counted once (seenG) and posted once from an unlocked copy (postedG) - before, each copy counted and the last copy in the page won at apply, silently dropping a tick under 5 GHz-1; RWFP_49 is rewritten to say what the boxes are and that a fixed DFS channel still moves when radar is detected; Extension Channel rebuilds its options per channel from the driver's sideband list (13 is Below only, 1 Above only; the composer already corrected an impossible pick, the page showed the other one); Fragmentation Threshold's help gains RWFP_83 (editable in Legacy mode only, as stock); Set AP Isolated leaves the page and wlpro_nv_fields loses ap_isolate - on this build isolation is a per-network setting on the Network menu and the per-radio key reached only the primary BSS. Efficiency items measured on the RT-BE96U on 2026-09-20: rc/rwarden.c start_rwarden() skips its synchronous apply.sh while /tmp/.reaper_firewall_built (rc.h REAPER_FW_BUILT_MARK) is absent - a tmpfs marker written by start_firewall()'s Reaper block (rc/firewall.c, under the re-taken lock, before the Warden re-apply) and by a completed apply.sh, so it is absent on every fresh boot and present for every later restart_rwarden; the boot-time run was about 6 s of pid 1 on the path to start_wan (the awk split of the 1.7 MB cache, the per-set ipset restore, the counter snapshot, 317 iptables calls) that the WAN-up start_firewall() tore down and redid about 15 s later; rc/rwatch.c check 3c words the no-WAN case (armed by the heal after HEALGRACE) instead of reporting a fault. rc/wanduck.c chk_proto(): restart_autowan once a minute while current_state is WAN_STATE_CONNECTED and on every 5 s scan otherwise, in the single-WAN branch only (dual WAN never reaches it) - the unconditional respawn was about half of init's idle burn (owner's test: 72 -> 38 cs per 15 s with wanduck stopped). rtrafd/rtrafd.c rt_bound(): the watcher forks its sleep, traps TERM, kills and reaps that sleep, and the main shell reaps the watcher, so a fast query no longer strands a sleep on pid 1 (seven per 4 s class poll, the other half of the burn; every init wake ran check_services' four /proc scans). rc/init.c init_main(): the two sleep 3 around the /data mount and bcm_knvram become reaper_mount_data() (a st_dev poll, the mount re-issued once a second, 10 s ceiling) and reaper_wait_knvram() (a socket(PF_NETLINK, SOCK_RAW, NETLINK_WLCSM=31) probe: the module's init is the wlcsm netlink family registration with no deferred work; /proc is not mounted yet at that point and this platform has no /dev/nvram); rc/services.c start_hotplug2() polls /proc/net/netlink for the process's NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT socket instead of sleep(1), and start_dhd_monitor() pays its 300 ms only when a previous debug_monitor exists. netool, sysstate and dns_dpi_check stay: each has a consumer on this build (Main_Analysis_Content and Main_Netstat_Content call /netool.cgi, the feedback report packs the /tmp/asusfbsvcs logs, the Bandwidth Monitor page starts dnsqd). Dictionaries: RWFP_67-83 added translated and RWFP_49 rewritten in all 25 packs, lockstep at 7036; the 33 English-seeded v3.2.2 tokens stay English this release (owner). Built and verified locally as RT-BE96U MCP test images (v3.2.2_BETA_r1 on the page commits, _r2 on the efficiency commit; reaper_verify 34 pass, 0 warn, 0 fail; the rt_bound harness under busybox ash: the old form leaves one orphaned sleep per call, the new form none, and a hung single command is still killed at the cap) before the cut. releases.summary: One Wireless > Settings tab (www/Reaper_WiFiSettings.asp) replaces the stock General and Professional tabs and the Reaper WiFiPro page (deleted); httpd/reaper_inject.c SUP-redirects all three to it and Advanced_Wireless_Content.asp leaves reaper_css_only so the bounce reaches it. Every radio setting a user can change is on the one page, a column per band, one restart_wireless per apply; network name, security, 11ax/11be and Smart Connect stay on the Network menu, where the SDN profile owns them. New httpd SSI wlpro_chanspecs() emits the per-radio chanspec list from wl<unit>_chansps (the prebuilt ej_wl_chanspecs fills it) so the channel and bandwidth rows offer what the driver reports, and they fold into wl<unit>_chanspec at apply exactly as the General tab did (2.4 GHz <ch>l|u plus wl<unit>_nctrlsb, 5 GHz <ch>/<bw>, 6 GHz 6g<ch>/320-1|2); wlpro_nv_fields grows to 37 keys. The scheduler edits a 7x24 grid and writes the V2 wl<unit>_sched_v2 off-time rules rc/watchdog reads on this build. The seven rows v3.2.0 removed are back, locked only where stock locks them: Legacy parks beamforming, modulation scheme, AMPDU RTS and RTS Threshold, WMM is a choice in Legacy only, Fragmentation Threshold is editable in Legacy only, MU-MIMO follows the OFDMA choice. A forced value is written at apply as a derived heal when nvram disagrees (WMM on, mumimo from ofdma, frameburst off under pre-emptive Bluetooth, txbf under MU-MIMO, timesched 0 under MLO), as the 11ax heal already was. The v3.2.1 Wireless Mode row carries over with its coupling (apply writes wl<unit>_11ax=1 whenever the applied mode allows HE and the stored value is not 1; a mode that drops HE confirms first). The radio toggle is refused off while MLO is on (stock check_mlo_status), the scheduler is parked while MLO holds the radios, and an AiMesh confirm precedes a radio-off in router/AP mode. No visible lock text: greyed is the signal. The enhanced select menus ignore clicks and scrolls inside the open list (a long channel list closed when its scrollbar was touched; WiFiPro had the same bug). menuTree carries one Settings tab; the dashboard rail and the WPS page's two links point at the new page. rc/rwarden.c: fold.sh and stats.sh take one iptables -nvxL / ip6tables -nvxL snapshot per run and parse TOTAL and every bucket from it by Chain section - the separate listings let a packet arriving between reads bank in a bucket but not the total, drifting the store a few packets per 15-minute checkpoint with Unclassified clamped at zero; the Warden page reads Blocked packets (RWDN_108) and a card under How Warden works (RWDN_102-107) says what the number is. Reaper_Traffic, Reaper_QoS and Reaper_QoSDiag use the RTRF_78/79 Download/Upload nouns instead of the CTL_upload button verb, which in Russian is the same word as the stock Download label (field report). Dictionaries: RWFP_40-43, RWFP_45-66, RWDN_102-108 and RTRF_78/79 added, RWFP_12 and RWDN_44 retired, all 25 packs in lockstep at 7019; RWFP_40-66 and RWDN_102-108 are English-seeded in the 24 non-EN packs and owed to the next translation pass. Version chosen over a v3.2.1 re-cut because the on-router update check compares X.Y.Z numerically and strips a trailing letter, so only a higher number reaches routers already on the v3.2.1 beta. Built and verified locally as RT-BE96U MCP test images (v3.2.1_BETA _r2 to _r6 on the same source, reaper_verify 34 pass, 0 warn, 0 fail) and flashed on the RT-BE96U; read back through the lab: the Settings page and redirects in the image, per-band chanspec lists populated (25/89/324 entries), Warden's banked total equal to its buckets, the Russian nouns in the dictionaries. releases.summary: Wireless Mode returns to the WiFi Professional page, per radio, with the coupling it never had. Every mode except Auto, N/AC/AX mixed and AX only makes bringup write wl<unit>_11ax=0 (no HE, so no EHT), and nothing in the firmware ever wrote it back - rc/init.c seeds the key only when unset and stock hides both the mode and the 11ax selects on Wi-Fi 7 platforms - so a radio once set to N only stayed at Wi-Fi 4/5 after returning to Auto (the 2026-09-18 badge report, and the reason v3.2.0 dropped the row). Option sets are stock's regen_mode(): 2.4 GHz Auto/N only/Legacy, 5 GHz Auto/AX only/N-AC-AX mixed/Legacy, 6 GHz Auto/AX only; the firmware has no Wi-Fi 7-only mode. Seven rows a user could not safely change leave the page: WMM (bringup forces it on in Auto), MU-MIMO (now derived from the OFDMA choice at apply, as stock does), explicit and universal beamforming, modulation scheme, AMPDU aggregation and Bluetooth coexistence (stock hides all of them on Wi-Fi 7; bringup consumes txbf, turbo_qam and mumimo). The radio toggle is linked to the surfaces that also drive it: refused while MLO is on (stock check_mlo_status), a chip on a scheduler-owned radio (wl<unit>_timesched joins the httpd snapshot, read-only), an AiMesh confirm before a radio goes off in router/AP mode; AMPDU RTS Disable parks that radio's RTS and Fragmentation thresholds. releases.summary: Policy Routing follows the order the rules are in. Every selector rule in the REAPER_PBR mangle chain now carries `-m mark --mark 0x0/$MASK`, so the FIRST rule to match a packet is the only one that writes a verdict. Before this, MARK did not terminate the chain and --set-xmark overwrote the masked nibble, so every matching rule ran and the LAST in the list decided: a broad source rule placed below a specific ipset or domain rule silently beat it. A field report on 2026-09-17 (RT-BE86U, v3.1.8_BETA) showed the asymmetry that gives it away - a client sent to a tunnel by a Policy Routing source rule stopped following its own ipset destination rules, while the same client sent to the same tunnel by VPN Director kept following them, because that path resolves by ip-rule pref (10210 against 9002) rather than by position in one chain. Rule count is unchanged, so rwatch's reassert check and the diag figure are unaffected, and the walker already models an `-m mark` match. Rule Status also names the stand-in addresses it walks with (new token RFW_322): the tab generates a LAN client at .123 plus an unclaimed WAN source and destination, sends none of them anywhere, and used to print them bare, which one tester twice reported as a device they could not find. releases.summary: One refused firewall line no longer costs you the whole table, and a box in Access Point mode is a first-class box. Field data from the RT-BE88U report (review R15) showed a router running on start_default_filter()'s boot skeleton for two weeks - no port forwards, no VPN server chains - because iptables-restore is atomic and one line the kernel would not take discarded the whole filter table, with the restore's own error sent to /dev/null so nothing on the box could say which line; reaper_restore_rules() now keeps that output, names the refused line in syslog and applies the table without it, and rwatch + the diag report recognise the skeleton. The GT-BE19000 tester's write-up and diag arrived and the decisive fact was unstated in both: that box is in Access Point mode, and three of the four items were Reaper surfaces assuming a routing box, in code every model shares - the socket-buffer ceilings that start_firewall() returns before reaching, the dashboard client tiles filtering on a networkmap flag derived from leases and conntrack a bridging box does not have, and an Internet card deriving its verdict from wan0_state_t and painting a healthy router red. All three are fixed by operation mode rather than by model, so a routing box is unchanged. Also: Warden's outbound total survives its own statistics window, Policy Routing greys a Status cell that is not a live verdict, a duplicate log_level default is gone, and the inherited-component list had its third in-code pass - netatalk's remaining 2022 set (CVE-2022-23125, -45188, -23121) and Quagga CVE-2016-1245 closed, wpa_supplicant and lighttpd retired on what this build actually compiles. The extensions now go only on the signing call (openssl ca never copied request extensions), and the repair path keeps its output and names the failing stage. DDNS: a dual-WAN router with IPv6 only on the secondary WAN failed the per-WAN address test on every run, which cleared ddns_ipv6_updated, which kept the watchdog's early return from ever being taken - a 30 s restart loop for the life of the boot; it now records the state (ddns_ipv6_absent), stands down, and wan6_up() clears it. releases.summary: Your Killswitch decides, and the firewall watchdog stops fighting a rule you meant. Policy routing realised BLOCK as an unconditional lower-priority `prohibit`, so a rule whose target tunnel went down failed closed whatever vpn_clientN_enforce / wgcN_enforce said on that client's own page - two answers to one question, and a disagreement with VPN Director on the same router. P3 in rc/reaper_pbr.c now reads the switch per target: on keeps the `prohibit`, off omits it and the traffic falls back to the WAN. BLOCK is still realised solely as `prohibit`; nothing else in rule generation moves. Saving a Killswitch restarts vpnrouting, so that restart calls the new reaper_pbr_regen(), which regenerates the COMMITTED rules in place - deliberately not start_reaper_pbr(), which unlinks the draft and would discard an apply still awaiting confirmation. Metal (RT-BE96U, 2026-09-11): wgc5_enforce=0 gives `9010 lookup wgc5` alone with `ip route get 1.1.1.1 mark 0xa0000` via the WAN; =1 adds `9110 prohibit` and the same command is denied - both from the nvram toggle plus `service start_vpnrouting0`, with no Policy Routing apply. Reaper_VPNRouting.asp stops claiming fail-closed for everything: the CGI reports each client's Killswitch (wks/oks), the chip on a rule whose client is off says blocked or using the WAN, the Target column names the interface, a LAN-wide accel bypass is badged, and Apply holds its overlay until the Keep / Revert bar takes over. rwatch section 3d required REAPER_HOOK_F at position 1 and re-pinned it every ten minutes; on a real network a LAN->filter DNS carve-out has to sit in front of it or Gatekeeper's per-device DROPs take DNS from every restricted device, and the two fought for 700 minutes (metal, v3.1.2, 2026-09-10). 3d now classifies what is ahead: a terminal target cannot bypass us; a user chain or a bare ACCEPT/RETURN is tolerated only when it narrows to a port or destination (`-s` deliberately does not count - restricting who may pass does not restrict what they reach); a chain that does not exist is broad, because unknown is not safe; and a chain named in /jffs/reaper/front_exempt is declared outright (a file, not an nvram list, which truncates silently at 1 KB here). Tolerated company logs once per state change and is never repaired; real drift still fails, and after two re-pins that did not stick the third names the file that ends it and stops. Confirmed on the same box and the same rmcpd_lab rule that raised a FAILURE on v3.1.2. reaper_diag reaches v1.3.14 with six counters corrected, each reproduced on metal 2026-09-10: conntrack re-read the live table per figure (405 entries against 510 by protocol) and now takes one snapshot; the syslog section counted the USB mirror and its source as two logs (12,360 lines against 5,634 distinct, ~2.2x on every count in the section) and counted the lab MCP's `exec:` echo of the operator's own commands (2 panics on a box with none); 'boots in span' counted syslogd starts, which a service cascade produces without a reboot, and is replaced by /proc/uptime - the only boot marker this RTC-less hardware has - with the syslogd figure labelled for what it counts; the panic pattern matched a bare case-insensitive 'Oops'; /proc/sys/kernel/tainted was printed raw although it is a bitmask (4097 = two flags); and RW_FDROP left the chain-counter list, since forward drops share RW_DROP by design and the probe reported it absent on every healthy box. Also in this rung: the Administration tab is renamed DNS Failover; the EDNS Client Subnet help text states that the complete client address is attached at receive time, before an upstream is chosen, so it reaches any public fallback used while the owner's filter is down; the two silent overrule paths in start_reaper_pbr() log when the file store and nvram genuinely differ; and the generated /tmp/rwatch.sh ends in an explicit `exit 0` instead of leaking the status of a log-rotation test that is false on any mirror under 8 MB. releases.summary: A WireGuard policy rule that no longer reboots the router, and a pre-release that says it is one. Broadcom's skip_wg_network and biqos /proc read handlers sprintf() into the char __user * buffer they are handed; with CONFIG_ARM64_PAN and CONFIG_PANIC_ON_OOPS that store faults and panics, so the router restarted about five seconds after Apply and Confirm. An empty table never reaches the sprintf and stock only ever writes these files, so the fault needed a reader with an entry present - pbr_skip_add in rc/reaper_pbr.c, only for a WGC target, which is exactly why OpenVPN, WAN and Block rules were unaffected and why rwatch's five-minute re-run turned one rule into a loop. Both read handlers now use simple_read_from_buffer(); both write handlers bound copy_from_user against the destination (128 bytes of kernel stack, previously unbounded) and NUL-terminate, and the 675x write no longer indexes tbuf[minsize+1] on a char[4]. Fixed in both platform trees and on all six models, with a new wg-blog-proc static check because the file sits outside release/src/router and the fix leaves no string a verify marker could pin. Also in this rung: every build is stamped _BETA in EXTENDNO unless built as `stable`, per variant, and the ship step stages a differing image under the next free _rN instead of skipping; rwatch 3d/3e add a chain-integrity watchdog (RW_DROP/RW_ODROP/RW_SDROP must end in DROP with no ACCEPT or RETURN; REAPER_HOOK/_F/_O re-pinned to position 1 under the firewall lock) and log which of the four causes of Warden outbound silence is in effect; the Firewall Logging viewer's classOf() tells WARDEN, WARDEN-OUT and WARDEN-SELF apart again and its table heads match its cells; the Addons rail item navigates instead of unfolding; DoT servers gain an optional strict failover order; and the resolver health check carries both an IPv6 and an IPv4 address for the server it watches. Two tree-hygiene commits are in the series' range but carry no code: 95a1ee8ac3 had been made from a warm build tree and added 10,110 build-output files across some fifty vendored packages, which took overlays/openssl-3.5-source.tar.gz from 50 MB to 108 MB (past GitHub's 100 MB limit) and would have exported a 217 MB patch. The accidental adds were removed before the export, so the archive is back to its 5,767 source files and 50 MB and the openssl-3.5 tree id is once again the one v3.1.1 shipped; a scoped .gitignore keeps that directory's build output untracked. releases.summary: A standby for the router's DNS list, and an OpenVPN certificate that survives a save. The Reaper resolver health check watches one LAN DNS server with a real query and, after a run of misses, moves it to the end of dnsmasq's upstream list and reloads; after a run of hits it puts it back first - so a filter such as AdGuard Home or Pi-hole can be the only DNS the router hands out without its outage becoming the whole network's. It gets its own Failover tab under Administration, beside three dnsmasq switches that previously needed a config-add file (strict upstream order, EDNS Client Subnet, router cache off). The health check takes an IPv6 server while IPv6 is enabled. Also in this rung: set_ovpn_key() no longer treats an empty GUI field as a delete instruction - the defect that silently destroyed a working OpenVPN server certificate on an unrelated save, unrecoverably, because the firmware only regenerates when the CA, key and cert are ALL absent - and a server found with its CA intact and its certificate missing now rebuilds only the server leaf from that CA, verified against it before install, so deployed client profiles stay valid. The firmware page's overlay escape button is a real Cancel during an upload and is withdrawn once every byte is sent. Gatekeeper resolves a multi-link client through the live list's mld_mac field, so a 6 GHz client is no longer shown as Wired or as two rows, and a band cached once and gone stale is corrected from this router's own view only. A device whose hostname dnsmasq gave to another one is no longer Unknown device: the lease script records each announced name per MAC, with a vendor-label fallback. The dashboard rail clock keeps its crimson seconds. releases.summary: Patches 0609-0620 (12 patches; the OpenSSL 3.5 source, 5,767 files, ships beside the series as the hash-pinned overlays/openssl-3.5-source.tar.gz that CI unpacks after the series). The firmware moves from OpenSSL 1.1.1w (end of life since September 2023) to OpenSSL 3.5.8: every source-built consumer (123 binaries: hostapd/wpa_supplicant, httpd, curl, wget, OpenVPN, strongSwan, inadyn, Tor, vsftpd, lighttpd, net-snmp, rmcpd and the rest) links libcrypto/libssl.so.3 directly; the closed ASUS binaries keep the 1.1 ABI through a forwarding shim (upstream Asuswrt-Merlin work by RSDNTWK, parallel-compile fix by Eric 'Merlin' Sauvageau, carried as cherry-picks with authorship intact); rmcpd links 3.5 alone. The withdrawn v3.0.3 attempt shipped a hostapd still bound to the 1.1 name (the wireless SDK's link rule never sees a library change), so this rung purges every object built against the old headers, git-ignored ones included, and adds release check 22 (check_ossl_consumers.sh) naming the only binaries allowed to depend on the 1.1 name; hostapd must link .so.3, verified with readelf. Proven 31 minutes on the RT-BE96U (hostapd never restarted, WPA3-SAE on 6 GHz at 320 MHz, HTTPS/TLS in and out, certificate unchanged). Licensing: OpenSSL 3.x is Apache-2.0 (LICENSES/, notices corrected). First boot is one box: Reaper_WiFiSetup.asp + reaper_wifisetup.cgi set the network name, Wi-Fi password and router login in one step, writing what the stock apply writes per band (psk2sae / sae on 6 GHz, Smart Connect on) and firing the same restart; the security banner is one row and one button (Set up this router); static check 9 locks the chain. Factory reset timing pass: prepare_restore skips the stop_app round trip when no USB app is mounted, both restore branches wait for resetdefault instead of the drop-after-15-s notify, factory_reset() takes ACT_REBOOT first so shutdn() cannot spin; syslog timers at each step; Reaper_Backup.asp's veil shows the open-factory-network rejoin hint, latches down only after five consecutive misses, and releases the page after three minutes if the router never went down; static check 10 pins it. amaspark reconciles the parked carriers against the live BSS state every tick and re-parks after any wireless restart. reaper_shell.asp collapses the rail into a sticky icon strip below 680 px; Connections page labels the scheduler SP; Advisor pin-IP hint no longer clips. The update check gains an opt-in beta channel (reaper_fwbeta, Firmware page switch): the manifest may carry a MODEL#VARIANT-beta# line written by a Dev-branch publish; a beta is offered only to a router already on the newest stable and only when its number is higher than the stable's, labelled on the page and the dashboard badge, with a -beta note; firmware before v3.1.0 never matches the line; static check 11 pins the chain. The QoS page stops explaining Weighted classes (removed in v2.5.4): RQOS_28 cut to its Priority sentence in 25 packs, the explainer block gone. Built and verified on the RT-BE96U (MCP, reaper_verify 25/0/0 incl. check 22; the 11 source static checks pass against the tree); that image (sha256 e28264fa...) is the beta test build.

releases.summary: One commit (patch 0554). Fixes a field-reported defect on v2.8.3: changing a Warden blocklist or pressing Update now answered "invalid request token", and survived a logout and back in. Reported from Firefox, but it was never a browser or a session fault - the request never parsed, on every browser. WHAT BROKE: when ban/allow/cfeeds moved out of nvram into /jffs in v2.7.9 (they had hit the silent 1 KB cap), Reaper_Warden.asp stopped putting them on the nvram apply form and began POSTing them to the new save_lists endpoint, building the body with `new FormData()` and calling send(lf) - which sets multipart/form-data. That endpoint's input handler is do_html_post_and_get, which is url-encoded-only and reads the body with a SINGLE fgets(): it got the multipart boundary line, which carries no '=', so init_cgi() registered ZERO variables, http_id was never present, and the CSRF gate refused. The blast radius was the whole page, not just the lists - rwSave() calls f.submit() only inside the XHR success callback, so the abort killed the master toggle, countries, feed selection and logging too, on both buttons. The live-stats poll kept working throughout because it sends the same token as a GET query string, which is why the page looked healthy while nothing could be saved. THE FIX is the transport, and it is the pattern already proven on applyapp.cgi by Reaper_Advisor.asp: URLSearchParams, an explicit Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and send(lf.toString()). The three values are single-line by construction (rwCleanCidrs joins on spaces, rwCfeedCollect on '<'), so no literal newline can truncate that fgets either; encoded worst case is about 34 KB against a 64 KB post_buf. SECOND CHANGE, because the report cost a round trip: the gate answered "invalid request token" for three unrelated failures, so one message could not distinguish a body that never parsed from a real token mismatch, and the user read it as a dead session. init_cgi() now counts the pairs it actually parsed (cgi_nvars()), and reaper_gate()/reaper_gate_hid() classify NODATA / TOKEN / XSITE. "request carried no parameters" (ek _1B) and "cross-site request refused" (ek _1C) are new; "invalid request token" (ek _1) keeps exactly its old meaning, so existing help text is unaffected. All 15 Reaper gates converted; the security decision is unchanged, anything but RGATE_OK is still refused. Two gates needed their own handling: the .rbk restore upload takes its token from a multipart field its own POST half captures, so it passes rbk_up.hid (an array, never NULL) and can only return TOKEN/XSITE - cgi_nvars() is legitimately 0 there; the disk-unmount endpoint reads a JSON body and emits no error text, so it refuses silently on any non-OK. Verified into the staged filesystem rather than off a green build: fs/www/Reaper_Warden.asp carries URLSearchParams with no FormData left, and fs/usr/sbin/httpd carries all three classifier strings. reaper_verify: 21 pass, 0 warn, 0 FAIL on both RT-BE96U variants. Confirmed working on hardware by the maintainer.

releases.summary: One commit (patch 0553). Closes the 2026-08-26 audit's Medium (17) and Low (14) remainder and fixes three defects found only while validating the earlier fixes on hardware. (1) THE WARDEN nvram->/jffs MIGRATION WAS DESTROYING LISTS: rc's nvram_safe_get() returns EMPTY for these keys above roughly 200-400 bytes while `nvram get` returns them in full (186 B read fine; 381 and 706 both came back empty; 602 B captured verbatim through the CLI in the same shell). The migration therefore wrote a 0-byte file and then unset nvram - the list was not truncated, it was gone, and the page reported success. Fixed two ways: rw_nvram_cli_get() reads through the path that demonstrably works, and the nvram originals are now DELIBERATELY KEPT so the worst case is 'did not migrate' rather than 'destroyed'. WHY the two read paths disagree is NOT established and is tracked separately; this rung removes the data loss, not the mystery. Proven on metal: a 912-byte, 60-entry list migrates byte-for-byte identical, the ipset populates to 60, and nvram still holds the original. (2) `%%` in an fprintf format string yields ONE `%`, so the generated shell carried ${LANIP%.*} where ${LANIP%%.*} was intended; LANNET came out empty and the Warden LAN anti-lockout RETURN was malformed. Found only by reading the GENERATED script on the router - a green build, a clean cppcheck and a passing staged-symbol grep were all blind to it. (3) rw_gen_apply()'s script ended on `conntrack -D`, which returns 1 when no live flow matches - the normal case for a freshly-banned address - so start_rwarden() logged the cold-boot 'LAN not ready at boot - protection deferred' on EVERY start with a non-empty ban list while protection was fully armed, making the genuine deferral indistinguishable from noise. The script now ends with an explicit `exit 0`. This one was unreachable until (1) was fixed: an empty ban list emits no conntrack lines at all. The Medium/Low batch also brings: atomic publish for the Warden update/fold/stats writes; a geo-fetch deadline so one slow custom feed cannot eat the window; ipset destroy-on-type-mismatch; the DNAT target restricted to a single IPv4 host; a CSRF gate on reaper_conn.cgi; LRU eviction and a pre-NTP grant refusal in gkd; a three-state exists flag in rjf_get() so an unreadable file is no longer indistinguishable from an absent one; rjf_syncdir() fsync-after-rename; a log-only proto-31 netlink socket-count detector in rwatch; and rexport's nine bare `nvram get` calls moved behind the _nv guard. releases.summary: Two commits (patches 0551-0552). Remediates a six-agent audit of the Reaper-authored surface - 2 Critical, 8 High, every one with a proven reachability trace. C1: rfw_gen_apply()'s teardown branch wrote apply.sh.tmp and returned success without renaming it into place (the enabled path does), so stop_reaper_fw() exec'd the PREVIOUS still-enabled script, rebuilt and re-hooked every chain it was asked to remove, then unlinked it - firewall enforcing, UI reporting it off, nothing left that could take it down until a reboot; introduced by ea085cdf16 (v2.5.1). C2: neither Gatekeeper CGI compared the target MAC against the requesting client, and the v1.7.3 $GKADMIN hatch was appended in the quarantine tail - after the per-MAC DROP and not at all when gk_default=1 - so blocking your own device severed the UI, SSH and LAN together with the captive page unreachable; the hatch now goes in ahead of the per-device rules and both CGIs refuse a self-block. H1: rmcpd's slow-read deadline was only tested once fgets returned a complete line and the request line preceded it entirely, so a dribbling peer parked the accept loop and held an armed session past both its expiry and a USB-key pull; bounded now with SIGALRM without SA_RESTART, which covers TLS. H2: del_iQosRules() flushes the whole mangle table and add_qos_rules() restores it without -n, deleting REAPER_PBR and its jump while the ip rules survive - selected flows fell through to main and left over the WAN in clear; reaper_pbr_reassert() now runs from the add_iQosRules tail and both HW-QoS teardown returns. H3: rjf_set() created only the last directory level, so with the engine off (the shipped default) every firewall list save failed ENOENT and the firewall half of an .rbk restore was silently rejected under a success banner. H4: rwarden_ban/allow/cfeeds were the last lists in nvram and hit the silent 1 KB cap near 63 CIDRs; they move to /jffs/rwarden behind a marker-guarded migration, the page POSTs them to a new reaper_warden.cgi save action and waits before applying, and export/import share one predicate. H5: the AiMesh window asserted a bare -j RETURN at position 1 of REAPER_GKI - above the cfg_relist exemptions and every per-device rule, so blocked devices regained access - and opened on cfg_obstatus=2, the ordinary AiMesh search; now REQ/LOCKED only and locally deadline-capped. H6: the self-heal throttle was a process-local static and the action it throttled respawns gkd, so the backoff was structurally dead and a persistent MISS meant a rebuild plus fc flush every 10-30s forever; the stamp now lives in tmpfs with a strike limit. H7: the export test ran synchronously from the single-process httpd select loop into an openssl s_client that -quiet makes -ign_eof, so a collector holding the session open took the whole GUI down until a reboot; detached with a bounded wait and s_client now exits on EOF. H8: a full conntrack flow table made every miss walk all 16384 slots - bounding the probe would have mis-credited a flow's whole cumulative counter as one delta, so an amortised compaction restores the empty slots instead. Reaper_Traffic.asp live charts are rewritten onto requestAnimationFrame with x derived from each sample's ARRIVAL TIME rather than its buffer index. The old lineChart placed points at x = 44+(W-44)*i/(n-1), so with the 120-slot ring full, one arrival translated the whole trace by exactly one slot - 956/119 = 8.03 viewBox units, 0.84% of the plot width - and the chart only ever existed at 1000/pollMs positions per second. Polling faster shrinks the step but cannot remove it, and it cannot exceed 10 Hz anyway: rtrafd rewrites live.json every TICK_MS=100 and httpd is single-threaded. Decoupling the two clocks turns poll jitter into interpolation. The Y scale was an independent second source: a raw per-poll max moved every point vertically the instant a peak scrolled off the left edge, so it now snaps to round values and holds before shrinking. Also: persistent SVG nodes with attribute-only updates instead of an innerHTML rebuild per frame, interpolated clipping at both window edges, and trace-breaking across a discontinuity so returning from a history window does not draw a ramp that never happened.

Main_ReaperDash.asp gains main{min-width:0}. .app is grid-template-columns:236px 1fr and main is the 1fr item, whose default min-width:auto resolves to min-content - the topbar's. .pills already carried min-width:0;overflow:hidden, but that only zeroes the automatic minimum once the container width is definite; during the track's intrinsic sizing the nowrap strip still contributed full min-content, so the DOCUMENT grew instead of the strip clipping. Measured docSW 1784 pre-fix, i.e. overflow for any viewport 1701-1788 CSS px - 1745 = a 1920 panel at 110% scaling, which is how it was hit. Below 1701 the failure was worse and silent: the responsive .pills nth-child(n+6/5/4/3) rules count the webs_state_flag badge as a pill, so the update notice vanished entirely under 1700. The notifier therefore also moves out of the strip to a full-width .fwbar banner at the top of .wrap, same #fw_update_badge id and same server-rendered reveal; FW_new_firmware_available and menu5_6_3 already ship in all 25 packs.

The file is therefore read as TEXT and never evaluated. internet_speed.html resets level_err_cnt at the start of a run. It was reset on a completed result (line ~574), on the silent-retry path in error_handling() and on tripping LEVEL_ERR_MAX, but never at run START, so the count carried across every test in the page's lifetime and a later run could begin with the tolerance already spent. A page reload cleared it, which is why it read as random rather than progressive.

SCOPE, stated plainly because the first draft of this entry overclaimed it: level_err_cnt is NOT a retry budget - nothing is retried. It is a tolerance for `level == "error"` entries in the ookla result buffer before the run is declared failed. The genuine single retry is speedTest_retry_done (986eb9f041) and the UI freeze was the sync->async poll rewrite (80fc8bfa88); this change is neither, and it does not touch why the binary emits error lines. It fixes exactly one pattern: later tests in a session failing sooner than earlier ones.

KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THIS RUNG: level_err_cnt is consumed once per POLL, not once per error. process_speedTest_result() runs every 200 ms until a type=="result" entry sets get_next=false, re-reads the whole buffer, and re-tests speedTest_result[length-2] with no index or dedupe - so an unchanged buffer counts the SAME error entry again every tick. LEVEL_ERR_MAX=50 is therefore ~10 s of a stalled tail at 5/sec, not 50 distinct errors, and that fits a FIRST-run mid-test death far better than the leak does. The fix is to count an entry once (track the buffer length at the last increment); the run stays bounded regardless because get_speedTest_result() already raises ERR_TIMEOUT at test_timeout. It changes how a run is bounded rather than when a counter is cleared, so it is not being slipped into a rung that is already cut. Recorded in docs/BACKLOG.md.

releases.summary:
Hot fix: IPv6 traffic is now counted per device in the Traffic Analyzer.

rtrafd's poll_conntrack() skipped every non-ipv4 line in /proc/net/nf_conntrack (`if (strncmp(line, "ipv4", 4) != 0) continue;`), so a client's IPv6 traffic reached the WAN and per-interface totals but was attributed to no device. On a box with a delegated prefix that is most of a modern client's traffic. Field report, RT-BE88U v2.4.3: 978.4 Mb/s on the WAN line against 521 kb/s shown for the device actually pulling it, while the window totals for an IPv4-heavy device looked correct - which is why it read as a per-device bug rather than an address-family gap.

The v4 path finds the device by looking the LAN source up in /proc/net/arp. IPv6 has no such file and no NAT, so either end of a flow may be the local device. Both ends are now resolved against the kernel's IPv6 neighbour cache via a netlink RTM_GETNEIGH dump (fork-free, mirroring arp_refresh()), restricted to neighbours on a BRIDGE - a neighbour on ppp0/eth0 is the ISP's router, not a client. Addresses are held and compared as 16 binary bytes, so nothing depends on conntrack's %pI6c text form matching inet_ntop's. Attribution keys on the MAC, the same key the v4 path uses, so a dual-stack device is ONE row. Router-sourced v6 goes to the Router bucket via the addresses in /proc/net/if_inet6. Per-network rings pick v6 up for free, so br0 and the guest bridges reconcile with the WAN line too.

The flow key and the byte deltas stay on the RAW conntrack tuple; only the presentation is swapped when the device is the reply side. This is deliberate: if the key tracked the credited end, a neighbour entry expiring would change it, the fl->key test would miss, and the flow's whole cumulative counter would be credited as a single delta - a multi-GB spike on one sample.

cli_t.ip is deliberately NOT widened. It is a 16-byte IPv4 field inside the persisted dbhdr_t, so making room for a v6 literal would change the on-disk layout and invalidate every saved history file (the DB_VER 1->2 precedent). A dual-stack device keeps its v4 address as the label; a v6-only device keeps whatever the network map gives it. top_t.src IS widened to 46 - top talkers are not persisted.

Also in this rung: the Analyzer's "By QoS class" panel now carries an Upload only badge (RTRF_75/76, English-seeded in all 25 packs). That engine shapes the upload direction only, so the chart can never show a streaming device's download, and the caveat had been buried in a FAQ answer. RTRF_45 is rewritten in all 25 packs: it still described the pre-v2.3.3 accelerator-table source AND told users IPv6 was not split per-device, which is now the opposite of what the code does. The 24 non-English translations of the old text were discarded rather than left asserting the opposite; retranslation is owed and is recorded in docs/BACKLOG.md.

releases.summary:
Security-audit remediation on the v2.4.2 rung, plus the v2.4.2 work itself, which published no images.

Before publishing v2.4.2 every surface it added was audited: the shell scripts rc generates and runs as root, the lines spliced into dnsmasq.conf, the JSON httpd parses, the new www pages and the rtrafd payload. Clean on the surfaces that mattered most - no command injection reachable in the generated scripts, no dnsmasq config injection, no XSS in the new pages, no new socket/daemon/setuid/system()/popen(), CSRF correct on the state-changing endpoints, and the new dict tokens safe in all 25 packs. Six defects were found, every one in code v2.4.2 introduced, and all six are fixed here. Each finding was re-verified against the source by hand before being accepted; three further claims did not survive that check and are not acted on.

httpd/web.c: rdev_amesh_is_wired() type-guarded levels 2 and 3 of its walk but not level 1. json_object_object_foreach expands to json_object_get_object(o)->head and that call returns NULL for a non-object, so a well-formed but non-object /tmp/allwclientlist.json - a bare [] parses fine - dereferences NULL inside a root process. json_object_from_file only reports PARSE failure, so nothing upstream catches it. Guarded at the function entry and at the caller. Latent: it first requires the ability to write into /tmp.

rc/services.c and rc/reaper_fw.c: the reader was char[512] against a producer that could emit ~838 bytes. Truncation is not a lost tail - fgets returns a partial line, the loop writes it, and dnsmasq gets a directive whose set list was cut, either naming a set that does not exist (an fqdn block rule silently never matches) or ending on a bare '/', which dnsmasq rejects and then refuses to start, taking LAN DNS and DHCP with it. Fixed at both ends: the producer builds the line in a bounded buffer (RFW_DNSMASQ_LINE_MAX 800, whole line <= 805) and logs any names omitted; the reader is 1024 and discards any chunk arriving without a trailing newline rather than emitting half a directive.

rc/rwarden.c: stats.sh used a fixed scratch path and httpd popen()s it on every 30-second Warden poll with no lock, so two open tabs truncated each other's chain listing and banked zeros - precisely the reconciliation confusion the v2.4.2 breakdown was added to fix. fold.sh had the same shape from apply.sh, stop_rwarden and the cron checkpoint. All three scratch paths are now per-process.

Three smaller ones: rfw_gen_dnsmasq ignored RFW_MAX_OBJ, which rfw_emit_sets honours, so past the cap it emitted ipset= lines naming sets that are never created and dnsmasq logged an add failure on every answer; the dnsmasq fragment was the only reaper_fw artifact written with no explicit mode, and rc runs umask(0), so it landed 0666 (now chmod 0600 before the rename publishes it); and two SDNs sharing one bridge - the IoT profile sits on br0 with the default LAN - emitted a duplicate JSON key in rtrafd, which parses with last-one-wins and relabels the main LAN series with the IoT network's name, so first writer now wins.

Two hardening items taken alongside: $LANNET is quoted in the generated destination-exemption rule, and resolver addresses read from /tmp/resolv.dnsmasq pass a VALUE gate before reaching iptables. The second is not a shell-safety fix - awk already guarantees no whitespace and both uses are quoted - but `nameserver 0.0.0.0/0` would be ACCEPTED as a RETURN at the head of RW_SELF, silently neutering the entire self-filter with no error for the `|| logger` fallback to catch, while every indicator continued to report it active.

Deliberately not fixed: /tmp is mounted 0777 with no sticky bit (rc/init.c, no S_ISVTX anywhere in the tree), which is what makes the httpd defect reachable at all. That is stock ASUS/Merlin behaviour affecting every subsystem including the closed blobs, so it wants its own rung and its own metal pass; it is recorded in docs/BACKLOG.md with two candidate fix shapes.

Warden enforcement, firewall usability, and two field reports.

Warden: direction out/both had never blocked anything. The whitelist was tested before the destination rules, and every outbound packet carries a LAN host as its source, so any whitelist entry covering that host - including the <lan>/24 entry this feature's own lockout guidance tells operators to keep - returned out of the chain before a single destination rule ran. Inbound blocking of the same addresses was unaffected, which is the asymmetry the report described. The destination group now lives in its own RW_OUT chain reached ahead of any source RETURN, and carries the loopback/LAN/own-WAN exemptions the destination side never had.

Warden also gains an opt-in RW_SELF chain on OUTPUT (nvram rwarden_self, default 0) so a compromised router cannot beacon to a flagged address; drops go to RW_SDROP, which always logs, and dnsmasq's upstream resolvers plus NTP are exempted so a poisoned set cannot present as a whole-network outage. It cannot lock an operator out: management is INPUT and the replies carry a LAN destination. rwatch reports self-drops.

The Warden block total and the country table could never reconcile - the total counts every drop while the table only ever counted the geo rules, and the feed rule is evaluated first (same drop target, so the order is attribution, not enforcement). THREAT and BAN are now banked alongside TOTAL/CC and the page shows the split.

The ten-minute resolver timer stays as the floor, since this only sees lookups the router itself answers. Every firewall tab also gains an explainer and a help link into a new docs/FIREWALL-GUIDE.md.

releases.summary: Single-change release: a workaround for a Broadcom defect in the closed libnvram.so that can permanently wedge an nvram write while leaving the router otherwise up. _wlcsm_init() passes the ADDRESS of its saved-PID field to the internal netlink port allocator as the port-candidate out-parameter; on EADDRINUSE the allocator walks ten candidates and writes each back through that pointer, corrupting the saved PID. The next call sees saved_pid != getpid(), concludes the process forked, and re-initialises without closing the previous socket - leaking one netlink socket per pass until all ten candidates are gone, after which wlcsm_nvram_getall() retries the failing send without bound while holding the nvram mutex. Because the send path re-enters _wlcsm_init(), each retry redoes the whole socket-plus-ten-binds sequence: roughly sixteen syscalls per pass with no backoff, which burns a core in system time, floods stderr, and never completes the write. The trigger is PID reuse landing on a netlink port a long-lived process already holds, and the leaked ports then squat for the life of the stuck process, so it compounds with uptime and process churn. Caught live on metal 2026-08-11 and confirmed instruction-by-instruction in the shipped binary. The fix is a small LD_PRELOAD object of our own (the closed library is not modified): it interposes bind() and, only when the real call already failed EADDRINUSE on an AF_NETLINK protocol-31 socket with a non-zero nl_pid, retries once with nl_pid = 0 so the kernel autobinds - which is what Broadcom's own second WLCSM socket already does. Every step of the failure chain is gated on that first bind, so making it succeed removes all of it. SHIPS INERT: /etc/ld.so.preload is global to every dynamically linked process and this has not run on hardware, so the nvram flag defaults to 0 and no router behaviour changes until an operator sets wlcsm_bindfix=1. releases.summary: Single-defect release: a framed-layout regression introduced by v2.3.3's own overlay re-anchoring, found on metal within hours of flashing it. Reaper_QoS.asp and Reaper_Traffic.asp rendered oversized and clipped at the right edge of a 1080p screen with no scrollbar. The v2.3.3 rule listed .flyout among the full-frame overlays and forced the whole list to position:absolute; the FAQ fly-out is not a full-frame overlay but a 440px side panel PARKED OFF-SCREEN at right:-460px. A parked absolute panel counts towards the framed document's scrollWidth and a parked fixed one does not, so the document reported +460px, the shell's frame-grow widened #page_frame to match, and every grid stretched to the wider frame - the 'zoomed in' symptom - putting the right-hand column outside the window. Only those two pages carry a fly-out, which is exactly why only those two broke. Fixed by keeping .flyout position:fixed while still anchoring its top/height to the visible slice; inside a frame that never scrolls internally the two resolve against the same box, so the fly-out still opens on screen. Measured alternatives, recorded so they are not retried: with an absolute panel right:-460px adds 460, transform:translateX(100%) adds 440, and visibility:hidden changes nothing - only a clipping ancestor prevents it, and clipping the framed root would break the deliberate frame-widening that lets wide stock tables pan. Second, .stage now carries min-width:0: it is a grid item whose default min-width:auto refuses to shrink below its content, so overflow-x:auto could never scroll and the page clipped SILENTLY instead of showing a horizontal scrollbar; any future frame-grow now pans visibly. Verified with a negative control in a mock render of the real shell, both pages - broken: doc 1603->2063 (+460), frame widened to 1603px, flyout absolute; fixed: doc 1143->1143, frame not widened, flyout fixed - matching the owner's on-router reading of doc 1405->1865 with ASIDE#flyout.flyout as the outermost offender. v2.3.3 was built and flashed before this was found, so the fix ships as its own version rather than redefining v2.3.3. NO IMAGES YET - this entry records the source rung; image hashes are added when the build ships.

releases.summary: Security + de-cloud rung, built and metal-validated on RT-BE96U. Every remaining admin-browser request to the ASUS CDN is gone from the files that ship on this model, verified against the staged filesystem rather than the source tree: client_function.js leaked the name of every ASUS-made LAN device out of the admin browser and wrote the fetched icon into custom_usericon (49 shipped pages load it; an earlier pass fixed only the dashboard copy, which does not ship); the AdGuard banner was fetched from the CDN with the bundled copy wired only as an error fallback, so every visit to that page announced itself before quietly falling back; collected_FAQ, DNS_List, extend_sdn_scenarios, ui-model-name, extend_model_icon, tz_db and pppIspList_V2 now treat the bundled /ajax/ copy as authoritative; GameProfile.asp no longer fetches from ASUS and no longer re-arms itself every 5 seconds forever on failure; Open NAT, IPTV and VPN partner-server lists resolve locally. Per-game artwork removed outright (104 rules, 414 lines) - publisher-owned game art hosted by ASUS, not ours to re-host in a redistributed image, and after the CDN urls were dropped every rule pointed at the same bundled placeholder anyway. QoS: the imq0 ingress redirect is no longer emitted for the hardware engines, where only the tc/HTB engine builds the qdisc it feeds - metal showed 4,619 packets through a redirect that could never shape anything. rexport: values reached a curl -K config unvalidated, where a double quote closes the url string and a following 'output = <path>' directive is an arbitrary file write as root; validated at the httpd layer plus a runtime guard in the generated script. rmcpd: ASUS '>'-delimited security tuples walked through the structural secret scrub, so a live PSK could reach an operator transcript via the lab exec tool. rwatch: the armed log line hardcoded /jffs/rwatch even when the dump root is relocated to the durable store. Native firewall Phase 1 scaffolding is carried but inert - reaper_fw.c is not referenced by rc/Makefile, the page is unwired, and reaper_fw_enable defaults to 0. Second cut of this rung (2026-08-11, patches 0380-0388), all browser- and accounting-side: the post-flash wait doubled its poll chain every round - a failed XHR fires both readystatechange and error, so each round scheduled two successors and the tab genuinely locked up after a firmware upgrade, which is the real cause behind the 'frozen browser' reports (an escape-less veil was a second, lesser defect fixed earlier). Framed overlays - Please Wait, countdowns, progress bars - now anchor to the shell's visible slice rather than the framed document, so they centre on screen instead of in the iframe's viewport. QoS ships the owner's validated classful profile as the type-11 default (rates, weighted/priority mix, class names, preset rules) and the DSCP map is corrected - CS4/AF4x had been landing in Streaming and CS3/AF3x in Gaming, inverted against the class names; preset rules no longer classify by transferred bytes, which had been demoting long-lived streams into the bulk queue. A stored XSS in the client-picker dropdown is closed: the value crossed two parsers - HTML-decoded into an onclick attribute, then parsed as a JS string literal - so HTML-encoding alone was the wrong escape, and a hostile DHCP hostname reached admin context; the last shipped ASUS URL went with it. rtrafd now takes its byte counts from conntrack instead of the accelerator's flow table: /proc/fcache/nflist lists only accelerated flows, so fast downloads - the ones most likely to be offloaded - were the ones most likely to be missing from the traffic list, and br0 under-reported. Plus the Network Map is retired with the dashboard taking its rail slot, the AiMesh node model name centres over its MAC line, and the firmware, Data Export and USB/storage strings are translated across all 24 language packs (dicts in lockstep at 6297 lines). NO IMAGES YET - this entry records the source rung; image hashes are added when the build ships.
